reason: While the text clearly demonstrates Abram's agency as a leader—receiving God's command, making decisions about whom to take (Sarai, Lot), and directing the group's journey—it does not establish that ONLY leaders have agency. The text mentions other individuals (Sarai, Lot, and the servants/souls acquired in Haran) who participate in the action. The verb וַיֵּצְא֗וּ (they went) uses a collective form, suggesting shared participation. The text does not explicitly deny agency to non-leaders; it simply foregrounds Abram's leadership role. The statement makes an exclusive claim ('only') that the text does not support.
